reason: The cited evidence (E1 on AlCoCrFeNi and E2 on CoCrFeNiMn) does not directly address the specific CrFeCoNiX system with controlled Al, Si, or Mn variations, nor does it provide data on oxide coherency, stress accommodation, or spallation behavior above 900 °C for these compositions. E1 describes mixed oxide scales and phase transitions in AlCoCrFeNi coatings, while E2 focuses on early-stage oxidation mechanisms in equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn, neither supporting the key premises about selective oxidation leading to coherent, slow-growing protective layers.
premises: Al or Si in CrFeCoNiX alloys selectively oxidize to form Al2O3 or SiO2-rich protective scales
These Al2O3/SiO2 scales are coherent, adherent, and slow-growing, minimizing lattice and thermal stresses
Mn in CrFeCoNiX alloys forms less coherent, mixed Mn-oxide scales
Mn-oxide scales crack or spall above 900 °C due to inability to accommodate stresses
Higher Al/Si content directly leads to stable, protective oxide, while Mn leads to failure
